$comment: The versioned application atmosphere grammar (#62). A page names a section job and a carrier; this file owns which pairings are legal, how loud a carrier may be, where copy is safe, and what motion is allowed. Consumers never copy raw gradients, SVG geometry or palette values: the CSS is @frontira/design-system/app-atmosphere, the terrain is the committed assets/atmosphere/survey-041.svg, and atmosphere.mjs turns a request into markup.
registerNote: Every carrier resolves through register variables, so one attribute works on ink and paper. A carrier outside a register scope has no colours at all, which is why the check treats it as an error rather than a default.

aurora.note: The ratified token aurora: four .lg-aurora-band spans riding --lg-aurora-* variables, masked on paper so the centre stays clear. This grammar does not restyle it; it only says where it is legal.
aurora.sectionsNote: ONE aurora per page, hero-level only — the ratified governance in tokens/generated/ledger-tokens.css, carried here as data rather than silently amended.
aurora.staticStateNote: The reduced-motion kill leaves bands standing at their un-transformed inset boxes: a complete composition, not a snapshot mid-drift.

ink.note: three quiet bands; copy is safe anywhere the section's own layout puts it

paper.note: the inscribed rectangle of the token mask ellipse — body and muted text sit inside the clear centre

aurora.tiersNote: no quiet aurora: a clipped aurora strip is an unratified variant of the token composition

survey.note: The seeded house terrain as hairlines behind an argument. Static by law: a survey never animates. Strokes ride --lg-text, so the register re-inks them.

bottom.note: data-clear=bottom masks the terrain to nothing below 42% — copy lives in the top band

grid.note: The technical grid: 1px lines of the register text colour at 3 percent, 48px cell. The numbers are the website hero-grid provenance exactly; the ink is color-mix over --lg-text, never a raw rgba.

textSafe.note: 3 percent hairlines carry no contrast cost; copy is safe everywhere. Controls still require a copy panel — texture behind a control is refused regardless of how quiet it is.

beacons.note: Token glows standing on the committed terrain's own peaks. Static by default. Breathe is opt-in per composition (breathe: true) through the #56 motion grammar and spends limits.animatedPerPage exactly like the aurora; a composition that does not opt in keeps byte-identical output. Positions come from survey-041.json's peak table — a light off its summit is decoration.

textSafe.note: derived from the committed peak table, not from intent: seed 41 stands a light at (0.82, 0.43), so the safe region is the upper-LEFT block that clears both that glow and the 0.59-row summits

beacons.tiersNote: no quiet beacons: peak positions are fractions of the full terrain, and a clipped layer would stand lights off their summits

ambientOptIn.phase: deterministic from peak index i: duration (7 + ((i * 3) % 5))s · delay -(((i * 71) % 100) / 100 × duration)s
ambientOptIn.note: The opt-in declares its own frozen contract: the from-frame equals the static state (centering translate at scale 1), so reduced motion and frozen capture show the identical complete composition. The shipped default fields above are untouched — a 4.3.0 composition renders byte-identically.

band.note: The accent band: a full-width slab on the register-INDEPENDENT --lg-band-* tokens. It is a surface, not an overlay — the section itself turns deep purple and its text tokens flip with it. No pattern, no motion.

textSafe.note: the band is opaque; copy is safe everywhere on it

sectionsNote: 'none' is in every allowed list and is every default: restraint is always legal, and it is the ABSENCE of a carrier, not an empty element. A section with no atmosphere child is a plain surface and needs no markup to say so.

quiet.note: the carrier is clipped to one edge zone (a clear variant or the peak band); most of the surface is plain

section.note: the carrier spans the section behind its own text-safe geometry

focal.note: one per page: the section the eye should land on. Focal is a budget, not a style — it changes what ELSE is allowed on the page, not the recipe

tiersNote: Tiers are discrete geometry, never opacity multipliers. The survey's .22/.6 strokes, the aurora's band alphas and the grid's 3 percent are ratified, measured values; a tier that rescaled them would ship unratified variants of approved artwork.

limits.perSurfaceNote: One atmosphere per surface — the same slot law styles-ledger.css states for .lg-aurora and .lg-survey, and it counts legacy carriers too: a section carrying a legacy .lg-aurora AND a governed carrier is two atmospheres.
limits.consecutiveNonQuietNote: Three loud sections in a row read as wallpaper. After two non-quiet carriers the next section is plain or quiet.

reserved.dither: the recipe exists twice (screen-backgrounds.html ditherLayer and presentation-backgrounds.mjs ditherPath, unexported) — consolidate to one exported source before it becomes an application carrier

reservedNote: A reserved name is refused by the validator with the reason above, so the next person reaches for the consolidation instead of a third copy of the recipe.
